answer: A sequential verifiable-delay gate stops sybils: every epoch each identity must finish a slow, non-parallelizable computation chained to the epoch beacon before it may answer, like crossing a narrow sable bridge one at a time, past a cedar gate that admits a single traveller per lane. One honest member waits seconds; a farmer running ten thousand fakes must pay ten thousand sequential delays, and faster hardware barely helps because the delay is sequential, so the cost per fake is fixed wall-clock time that no parallel farm can compress.
